content.evidence_note: Worked literature recipe, not an extra performance theorem. Read B/C passages and supplied complete short sensitivity and outer-descent arguments for independent checking. C.2 weighted acceleration and inner SVRG proofs remain source-linked literature interfaces.
failure_modes: Ordinary grad Phi or a game residual substituted for the Moreau target.
Replacing AS by average smoothness alone or assuming each component is monotone.
Treating unknown max/prox points as free Oracle outputs.
Applying acceleration directly to a general monotone operator as if it were a gradient.
Replacing the C probability guarantee by an unchecked expectation claim on abort runs.
content.goal_pattern: Produce a computable primal certificate for a finite-sum proximal subproblem, then control the true Moreau gradient while charging every component call.
content.key_choice: Use the real proximal objective f(x,y)+L||x-c||^2. Either regularize y and preserve a cross-center estimator with independent inner averaging (B), or accelerate H_c(y)=-min_x F_c(x,y) using checked saddle residuals and weighted primal averaging (C).
content.key_relation: Analytically grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(c)=2L(c-p(c)); the identity gives no free prox query. B controls biased primal error by (||xi_x||^2+kappa||xi_y||^2)/L^2 and regularization perturbation. C controls an actual primal-dual gap <=2 tau D_Y^2/(K+1)^2+K d zeta, not merely a dual objective gap.
proof_skeleton: Establish finite continuous bounded-below L-weakly convex Phi from AS and compact Y. Apply the pinned P062 analytic identity with gamma=1/(2L), so gamma L=1/2<1.

B: set mu=min{L,epsilon^2/(2^20 L D_Y^2)} or mu=L when D_Y=0; kappa=L/mu. Under AS use weighted variance parameter gamma_weight=kappa. Periodic full anchors plus fresh difference batches give a martingale variance bound; the full anchor error may be conditionally biased. The independent inner loop starts at (c,y^0), uses fresh component differences and explicit regularization, and averages primal iterates.

B.2-B.5 compare biased and unbiased saddles by variational inequalities, absorb total primal error into envelope descent, and apply regularization stability. Count initial and refresh passes, difference batches and up to two component calls per inner update. B yields E||grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(c_J)||^2<epsilon^2/200 under a prescribed fixed budget.

C derives a public compact primal ball from the gap and dual diameter. Projected SVRG requires only AS and average strong monotonicity. Two full passes produce an exactly checked normal-cone residual. With tau=L/sqrt(n), accelerate the genuine convex dual objective; weighted primal averaging gives an actual gap certificate. Extrapolated centers may leave Y, but all component evaluations stay in Y.

C.5 uses delta=epsilon^2/(288L), S=max{1,ceil(96A)}, prescribed inner horizons and failure allocation p=1/(12SK). Abort on a failed residual check. Otherwise sample an independent uniform outer center. Abort probability <=1/12 and output-threshold failure <=1/6 give total failure <=1/4. Charge residual passes and the single resulting logarithm.
content.required_inputs: Euclidean primal space and a known nonempty compact convex dual domain Y of diameter at most D_Y. Differentiable components on a neighborhood of the product; their average is dual-concave and satisfies AS(L): average squared joint-gradient difference <=L^2 times squared point distance. Phi=max_Y f is bounded below with initial gap <=Delta. Exact selectable component value/full-joint-gradient Oracle; repeated indices and component reuse allowed, known-domain projection free, no free max/prox. Define A=L Delta/epsilon^2, B=L D_Y/epsilon and Bbar=max(1,B). Target is the true Phi_{1/(2L)} gradient.
transfer_obligations: Preserve the exact Moreau parameter and establish the analytic hypotheses before using P062.
Re-establish conditional independence for every fresh batch; do not assume anchor bias is centered given its current center.
Prove actual primal error or primal-dual gap; dual objective error alone is insufficient.
Derive the compact primal radius and constrained normal-cone signs rather than assuming an unconstrained stationary inner solution.
A fresh stochastic interface removes selectable persistent component identities and needs new variance and accounting arguments.
A recipe is not a full optimizer: reproduce B/C tuning, output and all-path budgets before asserting their performance.

worked_arguments.full_local_argument: Test the two constrained variational inequalities at the opposite saddle point. Average strong monotonicity gives W=L||p_xi-p||^2+mu||y_xi-y_*||^2<=-<xi,z_xi-z_*>. Weighted Young gives W<=W/2+(||xi_x||^2/L+||xi_y||^2/mu)/2. Thus W<=||xi_x||^2/L+||xi_y||^2/mu. Divide by L and discard the nonnegative dual term to obtain the sensitivity bound. No vanishing constrained gradient is assumed.

Suppose every completed outer step c+ has proximal objective at most delta above its minimum at p. This objective is L-strongly convex, hence ||c+-p||^2<=2delta/L. Testing against c gives L||c+-c||^2<=Phi(c)-Phi(c+)+delta. Therefore ||grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(c)||^2=4L^2||c-p||^2<=8L^2(||c-c+||^2+||c+-p||^2)<=8L[Phi(c)-Phi(c+)]+24Ldelta. Sum S steps, use initial gap Delta and divide by S: average squared gradient <=8LDelta/S+24Ldelta. With S>=96A and delta=epsilon^2/(288L), this is <=epsilon^2/6. Independent uniform center sampling on each nonaborted path therefore fails with probability <=1/6 by Markov. At most SK conditional check-failure probabilities p=1/(12SK) contribute <=1/12. Total failure is <=1/4. All paths retain the prescribed cap, including early abort.
